system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Updated SPA and Disclosure Letter

I've reviewed the Seller's package against our playbook. It departs from our positions on nearly every material point, and several departures are serious. Below are the issues, my reasoning, and recommended pushback.

## 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Our position:** Start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is only a *conditional fallback* requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — **none has been given.**

This is the Seller opening exactly at our undisclosed floor. We must not accept it, and we cannot drift to it without Amelia's sign-off. **Push back to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** Do not signal that 20% is acceptable.

## 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **only the excess above the basket recoverable** (deductible/tipping-basket).
**Our position:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar recovery once exceeded.**

Three separate problems: de minimis is 5x too high, basket is 5x too high, and the "excess above basket" mechanic converts it into a deductible rather than first-dollar. **Push back on all three.**

## 3. Time limits — Clauses 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; and a sweep-up that any limitation applies to **all** Claims unless expressly stated.
**Our position:** 24 months general; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia's written approval (not given).

The 18-month figure again hits our unapproved floor — **push back to 24 months.** The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" wording is a drafting trap designed to pull Fundamental/Title/Tax/fraud into the general short period. **Reject** — reverse the default so general limitations do **not** apply to the carve-out categories.

## 4. Fundamental / Title regime
**Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the **same caps and time limits** as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
**Our position:** separate regime — 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

This is a significant and unacceptable collapse of the fundamental regime into the general one. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title claims at AUD 4.8m or cut them to 18 months. **Reject outright.** Insist on separate 100% cap and ≥6-year period.

## 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance — 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** apply to **all Claims of any nature.**
**Our position:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance — no one may waive this.

As drafted this would cap and time-bar even fraud and would bar reliance claims entirely. **Reject.** Insert an express fraud/wilful-concealment/deliberate-misconduct carve-out across all limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions. This is non-negotiable.

## 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller:** general/deemed disclosure of the **entire data room** (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and **publicly searchable records.**
**Our position:** require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

This is a blanket "data-dump" disclosure that would deem everything in the room (and the public registers) disclosed against all warranties. **Reject.** Require that disclosure be specific and fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Note para 1.4 also disclaims that anything was "required" — fine as a without-admissions statement, but it must not dilute specific disclosure standards.

## 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
**Seller:** no claim for any matter of which Buyer or its advisers **had knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.**
**Our position:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

The "discoverable" wording is a constructive/imputed knowledge bar — even worse than actual knowledge. **Reject.** Delete the blanket exclusion. If any knowledge concept survives, it must be actual knowledge of named individuals only, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

## 8. Bluefen consent — Clauses 3 / 6.3
**Seller:** reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied **on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.** Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** yet. Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) with conditions in cl 11.3.
**Our position:** require effective consent **AND** evidence its conditions (cl 11.3) are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.

This is a material customer (30% of revenue). "Consent on delivery" ignores the conditions in 11.3 — a consent delivered but conditional is not effective. **Push back:** make effective Bluefen consent *with conditions satisfied/evidenced* a hard Condition Precedent to Completion, not a reasonable-endeavours covenant.

## 9. Riverlark — Clauses 2 / 7
**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m facility released **following Completion.** Disclosure para 3: not repaid, no discharge included.
**Our position:** current payout figure, **direct repayment from Completion funds**, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **+ Amelia Frost approval.**

On a debt-free/cash-free deal we should not complete with a ~AUD 3.2m secured facility undischarged. **Push back:** obtain current payout statement, repay directly from completion proceeds, and obtain effective discharge of security. If any release genuinely must be post-completion, require an irrevocable payout/discharge undertaking from the bank — and that needs Amelia's approval (not yet given).

## 10. Employee bonuses — Funds flow / DD-005
**Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised in the funds flow.** Disclosure para 5: not in funds flow; on-costs (payroll tax/super) unaddressed.
**Our position:** the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.

Saying it's "a matter for the Seller" while leaving it out of the funds flow risks these costs falling to the Company (and therefore us) post-completion. **Push back:** make the bonuses and all triggered on-costs an explicit seller-funded line item (or purchase-price adjustment), confirmed in the funds flow. Quantify the on-costs.

## 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1 / DD-004
**Seller:** indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "adequate." Disclosure para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 open; **no independent verification** of non-payment; no receipt or assignment in the room.
**Our position:** broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.

The risk is title to SOW3 IP not vesting until full payment — a narrow dollar indemnity doesn't cover loss of the IP/materials. **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover failure of the Project Materials to transfer (not just the fee), while preserving the cure of paying the SOW3 fees. Do not accept AUD 180,000 as a verified or capped number — seek proof of payment and confirmatory assignment.

## 12. Export/privacy incident — Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / DD-006
**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material." Disclosure para 6: download link to an unintended external address, ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed, scope, or notification required; **no confirmed breach, no loss amount.**
**Our position:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation nor overstate it. **Push back:** require preservation of logs, a proper investigation, and ongoing updates through to Completion, plus a specific indemnity for the incident and its consequences (investigation, notification, regulatory, remediation). Do **not** concede it is immaterial, and do not assert a confirmed breach.

## 13. Sandbar supplier renewals — AUD 330,000 / DD-008, DD-011
**Seller:** three renewals of AUD 110,000 each are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure para 8: unclear whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
**Our position:** assess; **no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.**

Don't accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label unexamined, but equally don't reflexively treat them as Debt. **Push back:** obtain the contracts to assess terminability, accrual and whether they're genuinely ordinary course; classify on the facts.

## 14. Title evidence — Clause / DD-012
**Seller:** title evidenced by the Company **share register at DD-012.**
**Our position:** require **independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, **not independent proof.** Disclosure para 10 itself concedes DD-012 is "the source relied on" and that Buyer has not verified.

**Push back:** require independent verification — ASIC searches, share certificates, authorising resolutions, and confirmation of no encumbrances over the shares (relevant also given Riverlark security). An internal register alone is insufficient.

## 15. Tax / IP warranties
**Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."
**Our position:** Tax and IP remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep Tax/IP/Title/payment/covenant categories separate with no hidden general-regime override.

**Reject** the assertion that Tax/IP are settled. Combined with the "all limitations apply to all Claims" sweep (item 3), this is an attempt to fold Tax and IP into the short/low general regime. Keep them as separate open categories.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Action |
|---|-------|--------|
| 1 | General cap 20% | Reject; push to 25% / AUD 6m. 20% needs Amelia Frost authority (none given) |
| 2 | Thresholds (25k/250k, deductible) | Reject; 5k de minimis / 50k basket / first-dollar |
| 3 | 18-month limit + "applies to all Claims" | Push to 24 months; reverse the sweep-up default. 18 months needs Amelia approval |
| 4 | Title/capacity folded into general regime | Reject; separate 100% cap, ≥6 years |
| 5 | Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance over all Claims | Insert fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out — non-waivable |
| 6 | Whole-data-room + public-register disclosure | Reject; require specific fair disclosure |
| 7 | Buyer "discoverable" knowledge bar (8.3) | Delete; at most actual knowledge of named persons; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnities |
| 8 | Bluefen consent-on-delivery / reasonable endeavours | Make effective consent + conditions satisfied a hard CP |
| 9 | Riverlark post-completion release | Direct repayment from completion funds + effective discharge; any post-completion release needs irrevocable undertaking + Amelia approval |
| 10 | AUD 420k bonuses excluded from funds flow | Make seller-funded explicit line item incl. on-costs |
| 11 | Ironquay narrow indemnity | Broaden to cover IP/materials transfer failure; preserve SOW3 cure; don't accept 180k as verified |
| 12 | Export incident "immaterial" | Require preservation, investigation, updates + specific indemnity; don't concede materiality either way |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals "ordinary course" | Assess on contracts; no auto Debt/price cut |
| 14 | Title via internal register | Require independent ASIC/certificate/resolution evidence + no share encumbrances |
| 15 | Tax/IP "settled" | Reject; keep open and separate from general regime |

**Overall:** This draft is Seller-favourable across the board, with three especially serious items: (a) collapsing the fundamental/title regime into the general caps/time limits; (b) the universal "all Claims" limitation/non-reliance sweep with no fraud carve-out; and (c) the constructive buyer-knowledge bar. I'd lead the mark-up on those plus Bluefen and Riverlark, which carry the biggest commercial exposure (~30% customer and ~AUD 3.2m secured debt on a debt-free/cash-free deal).

**Two authority flags for the deal team:** the Seller has opened directly at our unapproved fallback figures on both the cap (20%) and the limitation period (18 months). We should not accept or drift to either without prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. I'd recommend confirming our opening instructions with her before we respond.

Want me to draft the mark-up/issues list in clause-reference form for the SPA turn?
=== END ADVICE ===
